acceptance: C logical streams use C independent database sessions and a versioned schedule with one outstanding query per session.
The measured interval includes all admitted in-flight work and only complete workload-family cycles can contribute.
The runner records completed work, active duration, fairness, P50/P95/P99 latency, status, cancellation, and separately attributable client/platform resource use.
The predeclared scored set uses complete repetitions and publishes all runs and dispersion; failed streams, cycles, or repetitions cannot be selectively replaced.

Timeout handling invokes a platform cancellation or isolation boundary and a bounded drain barrier; failed drain invalidates the repetition and quarantines its connection, pool, or execution context from later scored work.
An integration test proves a deliberately slow timed-out query issues no work after the deadline and cannot overlap a subsequent repetition.
The default mix excludes JOB and full TPC-Havoc while supporting a bounded admitted advanced-function mix; official TPC throughput remains separate.
context: Implements the proposed cross-benchmark score architecture. Preserve official TPC metrics as separate outputs. Numerical weights, size vectors, concurrency points, thresholds, and the M4 reference remain pilot hypotheses until methodology freeze.
description: Extend BenchBox's concurrent-stream infrastructure to execute deterministic finite batches across independent database sessions. Preserve one outstanding query per session, full result consumption, complete-cycle accounting, fairness and tail telemetry, and timeout containment.
